name: Caribbean Stud Poker
description: Caribbean Stud Poker is a casino table game based on 5-card stud poker, played against the house (dealer) rather than against other players. Each player receives 5 cards and must choose to fold or raise after seeing one of the dealer's cards. The dealer must 'qualify' with A-K or better for the hand to play. Caribbean Stud features a progressive jackpot side bet for royal flushes and other premium hands.

history.origins: Caribbean Stud Poker is believed to have been developed in the 1980s, allegedly by poker professional David Sklansky (originally as 'Casino Poker'). It spread through Caribbean cruise ships and casinos, reaching land-based casinos in the late 1980s and 1990s.
timeline: Late 1980s: Introduced in Caribbean casinos and cruise ships.
1990s: Spread to US, European, and global casinos.
2000s-present: Progressive jackpot side bet becomes a standard feature.
history.cultural: One of the most widely played casino poker variants globally.
history.evolution: Its 'dealer must qualify' mechanic differentiates it from straight poker. The progressive jackpot, usually seeded at $10,000, creates huge prize appeal.

setup.players: 1-7 players each playing individually against the dealer.
setup.dealing: Each player places an Ante bet. Optional: $1 side bet for progressive jackpot. Dealer deals 5 cards to each player and 5 to self, with one dealer card face-up.
setup.equipment: Casino table with betting spots. Optional progressive jackpot meter.

rules.objective: Beat the dealer's 5-card poker hand. Dealer must qualify (hold A-K or better) for the Raise bet to pay.
rules.gameplay: Ante. Deal 5 each (dealer 1 up). Player may fold (lose ante) or Raise (2× ante). Dealer reveals. Dealer must qualify (A-K or better). If qualified, compare hands; player wins 1:1 on ante, paytable on Raise. If not qualified, ante refunded, Raise push.
keyRules: No drawing â€” hands are played as dealt (5-card stud).
Players may NOT discuss hands with each other (house rules).
Dealer must qualify (A-K or better) for Raise bet to be in play.

strategy.basic: Always raise with a pair or better. Always fold with less than A-K. With A-K hand, raise if dealer's face-up card is A or K and you hold another A or K in hand.
strategy.intermediate: Optimal strategy: Raise with pair or better always. Fold with less than A-K. With A-K high: raise if dealer's up-card matches any of your other 4 cards.
strategy.advanced: House edge cannot be eliminated. The progressive jackpot side bet has very poor EV unless jackpot is extremely high (~$200,000+ for break-even on $1 bet with royal flush). Basic strategy reduces house edge from ~5.7% to ~5.2%.
tips: Never make the progressive jackpot side bet unless the jackpot is above ~$200,000.
Dealer qualifying rule means folding preserves 1 Ante unit vs risking 3 total units.
